title: Full-suite prefill chunk result: +11.4% weighted at chunk 2048, but shape-dependent (+15.6% at 4K, -4.1% at 512)
verdict: Chunk 2048 raises the canonical weighted prefill rate from 273.84 to 305.18 tok/s (+11.4%) on the full twelve-case suite, with byte-identical output. But the effect is strongly shape-dependent: +15.6% at 4096, +3.1% at 1024, and -4.1% at 512 where the prefill work is identical either way. Decode regresses at every shape. This qualifies and partially corrects the single-case ladder artifact, whose +18.4% was measured only on code-p4096 - the one shape where the change wins.
supersedes_reading_of: benchmarks/results/2026-10-04-qwen4exp-prefill-chunk-ladder/artifact.json (the ladder's numbers stand for code-p4096; its headline generalisation does not)
quant: mixed GGUF: Q4_K gate/up experts, Q5_1 down experts, Q5_K 2 tensors, Q8_0 5 tensors

protocol.sessions: both arms sequential in one session, same host, no other GPU work

scoreboard_metric.estimator: total prompt tokens / total prompt time, the same estimator as the recorded scoreboard rows
scoreboard_metric.tie_to_scoreboard: the 512 arm lands at 273.84, reproducing the recorded canonical weighted 274.1, so this comparison is directly on the scoreboard's basis

composite.definition: prompt prefill + 128 decode transitions, from the arm medians
composite.reading: 2048 is a net loss at 512 and 1024 once decode is counted, and a net win at 4096.

the_p512_control.why_it_matters: at a 512-token prompt the chunk cannot change the partitioning - the prompt fits in one pass at either setting - so the prefill work is IDENTICAL. Any measured difference is a fixed cost of the larger configuration, not a partitioning effect.
the_p512_control.result: chunk 2048 is 4.1% SLOWER on identical work, and the regression is consistent in all four cases: code -3.95%, general_en -4.48%, general_ja -4.46%, mixed_ja_en -5.26%
the_p512_control.mechanism: prefill_chunk_size feeds staging_token_capacity in plan_qwen4_exp_residency (hipengine/generation/qwen4_exp_gguf.py:112) and the scratch reservation in resolve_qwen4_exp_context, so configuring 2048 allocates staging and scratch for 2048 tokens even when the prompt is 512.
the_p512_control.consequence: a blanket 2048 default is wrong. The correct change is shape-adaptive.

correctness.determinism: both arms report all_cases_deterministic = true; every case has one distinct output hash across its three repetitions
correctness.cross_arm: on the ladder's code-p4096, 512/1024/2048 produced byte-identical output_token_ids (129/129). This suite's two arms were not diffed token-by-token across all twelve cases, so cross-arm bit-identity is established for code-p4096 and not asserted for the other eleven.

noise.chunk_512_arm: max prefill CV 2.25%, max decode CV 1.34%
noise.chunk_2048_arm: max prefill CV 6.57%, max decode CV 9.91%
noise.investigated: no warnings, no thermal or throttling events, no OOM, no competing process, and 84 GiB free host memory at the end of the session
noise.reading: the larger chunk is inherently noisier. This is a real property to weigh against the gain, not a measurement defect, but it means the arm medians carry wider intervals than the 512 arm's.

why_the_ladder_over_generalised: the ladder measured ONE case, code-p4096, which is precisely the shape where a larger chunk wins most. A single-case sweep of a partitioning parameter cannot distinguish 'this parameter helps' from 'this parameter helps at this prompt length', and the difference here is +15.6% versus -4.1%.

recommendation.but: a shape-adaptive policy that keeps a small chunk for short prompts and raises it only where the pass count actually falls, e.g. 512 below ~1024 tokens, 1024 for ~1024, 2048 at 2048 and above
recommendation.expected: captures the +15.6% at 4096 and the +3.1% at 1024 without the -4.1% at 512
recommendation.prerequisite: the decode regression is unexplained and must be resolved or bounded before any of this becomes a default, because decode is a first-class target of the same objective
recommendation.existing_machinery: GGUF_PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZES_BY_GEOMETRY at hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1151/__init__.py:1627 already implements a geometry-keyed policy, but has no entry for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next geometry, so it falls through

limits: One host, one model file, one quant, one execution profile, one session.
Two arms only; no arm was repeated, so the shape deltas rest on a single run of 3 repetitions per case.
The 4096 arm is not in this suite; its +25.6% single-case figure and its arithmetic divergence are recorded in the ladder artifact only.
The decode regression is measured at all three shapes but no mechanism was tested. Nothing here explains it.
No default, flag, kernel or dispatch changed by this artifact.
